You are an impartial grader evaluating whether a completed action satisfies a CRITERION. You will be given:
  - The VALUE extracted from a tool call or agent output (as JSON)
  - CONTEXT containing the user's request, the action's arguments, and the date when available
  - A CRITERION describing what the value must satisfy

Decide binary PASS or FAIL strictly on the criterion. No partial credit. Use the request and the other arguments of the same action to understand names, pronouns, abbreviations, and what the action is for. Accept different wording that communicates the same required meaning. Do not require a message to repeat its recipient's name. The request and criterion describe what should happen; they are not evidence that the agent did it. Do not supply a missing answer from them or from a different action. Fail when the completed action omits, contradicts, or leaves unclear a required meaning. Output ONLY valid JSON in this shape:

{"passed": true, "reason": "a concise explanation naming the exact supporting text or the exact missing requirement"}

No prose, no markdown fences.

VALUE (as JSON):
"Recorded September 14, 2026\n\nIn my January 20, 2023 assessment, Marcus's 1:1 was going well. He was thinking more deeply about the on-call rotation than I had asked him to, in a constructive way. He had identified handoff gaps and a recurring pager mistake that kept happening around 2 a.m. Overall, my assessment was that he was settling into the team well and beginning to improve how we understood and handled on-call work.\n\nSource date: January 20, 2023."

CONTEXT: {"user_request": "Create an engineering-history note recalling my January 2023 assessment of Marcus's early on-call work.", "today": "2026-09-14", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Engineering history \u2014 Marcus's early on-call work (January 2023)", "body": "Recorded September 14, 2026\n\nIn my January 20, 2023 assessment, Marcus's 1:1 was going well. He was thinking more deeply about the on-call rotation than I had asked him to, in a constructive way. He had identified handoff gaps and a recurring pager mistake that kept happening around 2 a.m. Overall, my assessment was that he was settling into the team well and beginning to improve how we understood and handled on-call work.\n\nSource date: January 20, 2023.", "folder": "engineering-history"}, "field_being_checked": "result.document.body"}

CRITERION:
Records a positive early-ramp assessment: Marcus proactively examined on-call rotation and identified handoff gaps and a recurring overnight pager mistake. Does not claim he already fixed those problems.

Return the JSON verdict now.

{"passed":true,"reason":"The note positively describes Marcus as settling in well, thinking proactively and constructively about the on-call rotation, and identifying handoff gaps plus a recurring 2 a.m. pager mistake; it does not claim he fixed those problems."}
